reading: The grid's outer ring of cells (first/last row and column) is painted 8; the inside stays 0.

new_rows.name: edge_ring
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- px(Y, X, C).
edge_ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
edge_ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), X = 0.
edge_ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
edge_ring(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), maxx(M), X = M.

why: every grid-border cell is 8 in the output and every interior cell is unchanged

reading: The seed row's coloured cells sit at positions 0,1,3; the row is continued with cells at triangular positions (gaps 1,2,3,4,...) cycling through the seed's colours in order.

slots.seed: the non-zero cells of the middle row (colours in left-to-right order)
slots.positions: triangular numbers 0,1,3,6,10,15,21,28,... up to the row end

why: every non-zero output cell is at a triangular index and its colour is seed[i mod n]
invariants: rows other than the seed row stay 0

reading: Each odd-coloured cell inside the line of 1s grows a stalk upward: 1s then the odd colour on top; 8 gives a stalk of height 3, 2 gives height 4.

slots.line: the full row of 1s with odd cells
slots.stalk: (length-1) cells of 1 directly above the source, topped by one cell of the source colour

why: above every odd cell there is a vertical run of 1s ending in the odd colour, of the colour's fixed length; nothing else changes

reading: Every 4 moves down one row; any 4 that lands directly on top of the 2-line shoots diagonal rays of 4 up-left and up-right to the grid edge.

slots.subject: all 4 cells
slots.trigger: landing cell directly above the row of 2s
slots.rays: two diagonals (up-left, up-right) of 4 from the landed cell to the border

why: each input 4 at (y,x) is at (y+1,x) in the output, and only those touching the separator emit a V of diagonals

reading: In the columns shared by the top bar and the bottom bar, the cells between the 2-separator and the wider of the two bars are filled with 4.

new_rows.name: overlap_half
new_rows.datalog:
maxy(max(Y)) :- px(Y, X, C).
sep(Y) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y > 0, maxy(M), Y < M.
topc(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), Y = 0.
botc(X) :- cell(Y, X, C), maxy(M), Y = M.
topw(count(X)) :- topc(X).
botw(count(X)) :- botc(X).
both(X) :- topc(X), botc(X).
overlap_half(Y, X) :- both(X), px(Y, X, C), sep(S), Y > S, maxy(M), Y < M, topw(A), botw(B), B > A.
overlap_half(Y, X) :- both(X), px(Y, X, C), sep(S), Y < S, Y > 0, topw(A), botw(B), A > B.

why: exactly the overlap columns on the wider bar's side of the separator become 4; nothing else changes

reading: The 2s form a boundary across the grid; everything on the lower (bottom-left) side becomes the scatter colour, everything on the upper (top-right) side becomes 0, and the 2s stay.

slots.lower side: non-2 cells 4-connected to the bottom-left corner without crossing 2 -> filled with the grid's other colour
slots.upper side: non-2 cells 4-connected to the top-right corner -> cleared to 0

why: the 2s cut the grid into exactly two regions; lower is solid colour, upper is empty

reading: The scattered cells of one colour are removed and, as a group, fill the open cup of the other-colour shape whose interior capacity equals their count; other cups stay empty.

slots.filler: the scattered single cells (their colour and count N)
slots.cups: V/U-shaped objects of the other colour
slots.target: the cup whose enclosed interior has exactly N cells
slots.result: target interior painted the filler colour; scattered cells set to background

why: number of filled cells equals number of removed scattered cells, and they exactly fill one cup's interior

reading: The 7x7 block of 1s is a key with a colour at each inner corner; the output is a 7x7 grid where each 3x3 shape is placed in the quadrant whose key corner has its colour, with an empty middle row and column.

slots.key: the 7x7 box of 1 with colours at (1,1),(1,5),(5,1),(5,5)
slots.pieces: the four 3x3-box shapes elsewhere, one per key colour
slots.layout: piece of key colour at (1,1) -> output rows 0-2 cols 0-2; (1,5) -> rows 0-2 cols 4-6; (5,1) -> rows 4-6 cols 0-2; (5,5) -> rows 4-6 cols 4-6

why: each output quadrant is exactly the 3x3 box of the piece matching that key corner

reading: The 2x2 block of 6 sits in one 2-wide band; its own band is kept, and in every other band the 8s outside a widening cone around the block's rows/columns turn 4 (band at distance d keeps the block's span plus 2(d-1) on each side).

slots.bands: 2-wide stripes of 8 separated by 0 lines (rows or columns)
slots.kept: cells in the anchor's band, or within the anchor span widened by 2(d-1) per side at band distance d

why: only 8 cells change, to 4, exactly outside the cone; 0 holes and 6 unchanged

reading: A reference line inside a frame is compared cell by cell with a parallel line of coloured marks; marks equal to the reference cell beside them move next to the frame, marks that differ move to the opposite grid edge.

slots.reference: the coloured line inside the frame (row or column)
slots.marks: the parallel line of coloured cells outside the frame
slots.match: mark colour equals reference colour at the same position -> moved to the cell adjacent to the frame
slots.mismatch: -> moved to the far grid border line

why: every mark keeps its position along the line; its new depth depends only on whether it matches the reference
